harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s billing accumulator. It now sums nonnegative decimal counters with arbitrary precision on Python 2.5/i686, rejects invalid or negative records with no stdout, and persisted across a verified node restart. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Removed the forced 32-bit wrap and signed reinterpretation.
Implemented Python 2.5-compatible arbitrary-precision accumulation using long integers.
Added strict decimal validation with nonzero exit status and no partial total output.
Preserved the executable file interface, decimal output, ownership, and mode.
Verified ordinary, >4 GiB, extremely large, leading-zero, negative, malformed, and signed-text inputs.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed and application/service health recovered.

evidence.requirement: Sum nonnegative decimal counters exactly, including totals larger than 4 GiB
evidence.summary: The production fixture returns 4294967303, a dedicated >4 GiB case returns 4294967301, and a 31-digit total is exact. Results remained correct after restart.

evidence.requirement: Reject invalid or negative records without publishing a partial total
evidence.summary: Negative, malformed, and signed-text records return status 1 with STDOUT_BYTES=0; rejection persisted after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep counters and integer-decimal output interface intact and support the installed architecture
evidence.summary: Verified Python 2.5.1 on i686, successful syntax compilation, executable mode 755, file-input interface, and plain integer-decimal output.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged after implementation and restart.

Healthy baseline boot b3fea13b-bbfc-49ca-b5eb-270bddd4c124; reboot acknowledged; new boot fb2b44bb-fa6a-4577-b262-0f45a9a857ea; SSH listener, repaired checksum, production data, >4 GiB calculation, and rejection behavior all recovered.
